newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Bank of Israel cuts rate 0.3 point to 15.5 pct.
newsitem.headline: Bank of Israel cuts rate 0.3 point to 15.5 pct.

text.p: The Bank of Israel said it would cut its key lending rate for October by 0.3 percentage point to an annualised nominal rate of 15.5 percent.
The rate is for daily and weekly monetary tenders for loans to commercial banks.
The central bank noted it has cut its key lending rate by 1.5 percentage points since August. This is the third consecutive rate cut.
The decision follows an announcement earlier this month that the consumer price index (CPI) rose only 0.4 percent in August and M1 money supply grew only 0.1 percent.

A central bank spokesman said the decision was taken in light of mixed trends. On the one hand the CPIs in the last two months were low and the rate of expansion in M1 has been in line with economic growth. On the other hand, inflation is still running at a rate above the government's 1996 target of 8-10 percent and inflationary expectations in the capital markets for the next 12 months are still above the target as well.
After falling in the last two months inflationary expectations have stabilised at 11 percent.
The Bank of Israel stressed that a steeper cut would not be prudent, given the high level of demand in the economy and the need to narrow the current account deficit in the balance of payments.
The spokesman said a significant cut in the government's budget was needed to improve the current account deficit given the very large budget deficit in 1996.
